description: Warm-up label-swap series (factual), right variant. Identical to bike_factual_obvious_right except that every label is swapped: the first speaker is now Participant B, and the flawed message (message 4) is by Participant A. Text and planted problem are unchanged. Expected: the label letter makes no difference.

topic.title: Bike lanes
topic.proposition: Cities should build protected bike lanes even when it means removing some street parking.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: I support building protected bike lanes even when that means removing some parking, and I think a street is public space that should serve the people who use it, not just those who store a car on it. A lane with a physical barrier may make riding feel safe enough for people who now stay away, and safer streets may help drivers. I would rather see cities make that trade openly than avoid it. The change has a price, but perhaps it is a price worth paying.

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: Safe riding is a fair goal, and I agree that a barrier may help riders feel protected, but I think many shops and residents depend on parking near their doors. A quieter parallel street can offer much of the safety without taking any space from anyone, so the route may matter more than the barrier. Would a design that keeps parking for customers on the busiest shopping blocks be acceptable to you?

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: Keeping parking on the busiest blocks helps, but I think those blocks are often where riders face the most traffic, so the danger would stay where it is greatest. A network with gaps may not feel safe enough for people to start riding. I worry that the plan protects the shops more than any rider. Do you think cities with large networks tell us anything about ours?

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: Fair question, and I think it depends on the details and the place. Copenhagen, the capital of Sweden, has built a large network of protected lanes that people use, but I think a city like ours would face a harder road. That is why I would still keep the parking.

planted.correction: Copenhagen is the capital of Denmark, not Sweden; the capital of Sweden is Stockholm.
